**Getting OpenCode running inside the Codespace:**
1. **Codespace terminal** (`` Ctrl+` ``), from any directory — install is a one-liner: ```bash curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/install | bash ``` This drops the `opencode` binary somewhere on PATH (usually `~/.opencode/bin` or similar — the installer prints where and adds it to your shell profile).

3. **Auth / model access** — OpenCode itself is just the agent harness; it needs an LLM behind it. Run: ```bash opencode auth login ``` This walks you through connecting a provider (Anthropic API key, OpenRouter, etc.). It'll prompt for the API key interactively — paste it when asked. Set this once per Codespace; **Codespaces are ephemeral by default**, so if you rebuild/recreate the Codespace later, you may have to re-auth unless you set it as a Codespaces secret (see step 6).
4. **Launch it scoped to `/workspaces`, not just your repo** — this is the part that matters for the sibling-folder plan: ```bash cd /workspaces opencode ``` Starting it from `/workspaces` (rather than from inside `Obsidian-Seek-MCP/`) means its working context includes all three sibling repos once they're cloned. If OpenCode has a project/root flag (check `opencode --help`) you can also pin it explicitly instead of relying on cwd.
5. **Sanity check it can actually see all three repos** — once inside the OpenCode session, just ask it directly: *"list the top-level folders you can see in /workspaces"* — confirms scope before you trust it with real work.
6. **Optional but worth it: don't re-type the API key every Codespace rebuild.** Go to the repo on GitHub → Settings → Secrets and variables → **Codespaces** → New repository secret → name it something like `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. Then the clone should work.
**Permanent fix, for future Codespaces on this repo:** add the other repos your Codespace needs to a `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json` in `Obsidian-Seek-MCP` with: ```json { "customizations": {}, "containerEnv": {}, "features": {} } ``` — actually the relevant bit is a top-level `"repositories"` permission config, but simplest is just setting it in the repo's Codespaces settings on GitHub.com: **Settings → Codespaces → repository permissions**, where you can grant the Codespace access to specific additional repos (`system-vault`, `Obsidian-Seek`) at creation time so you don't hit this every time you spin up a new one.
